paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus is alive, and He comes to find people who are still looking for a body. Mary was at the tomb in the dark, weeping, sure the Lord had been carried off. Even the two disciples who ran in and saw the cloths didn't understand yet, because, as John says, "they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead." (John 20:9) Sometimes we just don't see it yet, and that's okay, because Jesus isn't done with us.

Now here's the part that gets me. Mary talks to Jesus and doesn't know it's Him, and what opens her eyes is not a speech. He says one word: "Mary." (John 20:16) He knows her by name, right in the middle of her tears. I think that's the heart of it, friend: the risen Lord isn't a far-off idea, He knows you personally, and He called me out of a junk drawer the same way, so I can tell you He doesn't lose track of anybody.

And look at what Jesus does next. He sends Mary with a message for His brothers: "I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God." (John 20:17) Then Mary goes and announces, "I have seen the Lord!" (John 20:18) Meeting the risen Jesus turns weeping into telling, so when He finds you in the Word, don't keep it to yourself. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story isn't over.
